title: Microcopy and progressive disclosure for batching/cache guardrail onboarding
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Teams enable automatic batching and prefix/KV caching but report confusion about when the system will apply recommendations and how guardrails will affect latency-sensitive routes. Hypothesis: A progressive disclosure onboarding that combines bite-sized microcopy, lightweight examples, and a guardrail toggle will increase safe adoption and reduce support tickets. Proposed solution: 1) Add a first-run spotlight in the Batch & Cache config panel showing 3 short tips (what batching does, what prefix caching is, when guardrails kick in). 2) Surface inline microcopy next to each recommendable control: short one-line explanation + a link for advanced examples. 3) Introduce an opt-in "safe mode" toggle (default on) that explains rate/latency trade-offs and sets conservative thresholds; provide a clear pill showing current effective policy (e.g., "Safe mode: conservative batching - best for latency"). 4) Provide two alternative microcopy variants for A/B test: Variant A = performance-forward language; Variant B = cost-savings-first language. 5) Add a small animated example that simulates latency and cost with the current config. Goals: increase enablement for recommended configs by 20%, reduce related support threads by 30% in 8 weeks, and keep error rates below current baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype for spotlight and inline microcopy reviewed by PM and Eng
Two microcopy variants implemented in prototype and instrumented for A/B testing
Guardrail toggle UI with descriptive pill and tooltip implemented in design spec
Animation/storyboard for simulated latency/cost included in prototype and accessible
Design handoff assets (tokens, states, copy, aria labels) uploaded to Drive and Figma components created

decisions: Default to 'Safe mode' on first-run to protect latency-critical routes
Use short one-line microcopy with an inline 'Why this matters' explainer panel rather than long paragraphs
Provide two copy variants for A/B testing: Performance-first vs Cost-first
Animation will be a short mocked simulation with pause/play controls and a link to 'raw numbers' for users who want deterministic data
